common_distractors: reporting the plotted function value as the limit
reporting one of the two one sided values as the two sided limit
answering that the limit is the open circle height when a closed point sits elsewhere
answering that the limit does not exist merely because the function is undefined there
archetypes.description: A graph of a function with one or more breaks is given and the response reports two sided and one sided limits and function values at named inputs, or states that a limit does not exist.
difficulty_variables: whether a removable and a jump break appear on the same graph
whether the function value at a break is marked
whether a nonexistence answer must be justified
whether an infinite branch is included
expected_solution_path: locate the named input on the horizontal axis
read the output approached from the left
read the output approached from the right
compare the two and report the limit or its nonexistence
read the plotted function value separately when it is asked for
archetypes.invariant_structure: The graph carries at least one input where the limit and the function value differ and at least one input where the one sided limits differ; every requested value is read from the picture without computation.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item or one part of a larger question.
archetypes.name: Limit estimated from a graph including one sided values
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Reading points are awarded per requested value, with a separate point for a stated reason when nonexistence must be justified. No official free response part in 2023 to 2025 assesses this task in isolation, so the pattern is drawn from the CED description of the topic.
typical_wording: Using the graph of f shown, find the stated limits or explain why a limit does not exist.

common_distractors: reading the output at the row nearest the target as the limit
averaging the two nearest outputs
reporting a value the table only approaches on one side
treating an estimate as an exact value
archetypes.description: Selected values of a function at inputs approaching a target from both sides are tabulated and the response reports the estimated limit, or a one sided estimate, from the table.
difficulty_variables: whether the two sides agree
whether only one side is tabulated
whether the table is deliberately inconclusive
whether units are demanded
expected_solution_path: identify the rows approaching from the left
identify the rows approaching from the right
state the value the outputs approach on each side
report the estimate or state that the table does not settle the question
archetypes.invariant_structure: The tabulated inputs approach the target from both sides without reaching it, and the outputs are given to a fixed number of decimal places so that the estimate is read rather than computed exactly.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Limit estimated from a table of values
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the estimate, with a separate point when an explanation of the limitation of a table is demanded. No official free response part in 2023 to 2025 assesses this task in isolation.
typical_wording: Selected values of f are given in the table. Estimate the stated limit or explain why the table does not determine it.

common_distractors: applying the quotient theorem when the denominator limit is zero
composing in the wrong order
adding when a product is requested
asserting that a limit of a quotient is the quotient of the function values
archetypes.description: The limits of two functions at a point are supplied and the response evaluates the limit of a sum, difference, product, quotient, or composite built from them.
difficulty_variables: whether the denominator limit is zero
whether a composite is involved
whether one of the supplied limits is one sided
whether the answer must be justified by naming the theorem
expected_solution_path: record the supplied limits
identify the combination requested
check the denominator condition when a quotient is requested
apply the theorem and report the value
archetypes.invariant_structure: The individual limits are given rather than computed, and the task is the correct selection and application of the limit theorem, including the denominator condition for a quotient.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Limit evaluated by limit theorems from given limits or tabulated values
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the value, with the denominator condition expected in a justified response. No official free response part in 2023 to 2025 assesses this task in isolation.
typical_wording: Given the stated limits of f and g at the named input, find the limit of the indicated combination.

common_distractors: reporting zero because the numerator tends to zero
reporting that the limit does not exist on seeing zero over zero
cancelling a term rather than a factor
dropping the sign introduced by the conjugate
archetypes.description: A quotient that gives zero over zero under substitution is presented and the response rewrites it into an equivalent form and evaluates the limit.
difficulty_variables: factoring against conjugate against complex fraction against identity
whether the factor to be divided out is repeated
whether the target is a boundary of a piecewise rule
whether the response must state the indeterminate form explicitly
expected_solution_path: substitute and observe the indeterminate form
rewrite the expression into an equivalent form
divide out the common factor or simplify
evaluate the simplified expression at the target
archetypes.invariant_structure: Substitution produces zero over zero, the rewriting step is available without calculus, and the rewritten expression agrees with the original for all inputs near the target other than the target itself.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item or one part of a larger question.
archetypes.name: Indeterminate limit resolved by algebraic rewriting
archetypes.official_examples_notes: 2023 Q4(c) treats the same indeterminate form through L'Hospital's rule rather than algebraic rewriting
safe_variables: the specific polynomial, radical, or trigonometric expression
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A response that presents a limit explicitly set equal to zero over zero does not earn the point for identifying the form; the form is established by presenting the two limits separately (sg-23:14). Remaining points are for the rewriting and for the value.
typical_wording: Find the value of the given limit, or show that it does not exist.

common_distractors: multiplying the inequality by a factor that changes sign without reversing it
evaluating the bounds at the target rather than taking their limits
concluding from a bound on one side only
omitting the statement that the bounds share a limit
archetypes.description: A function trapped between two bounding functions is presented and the response verifies the bounding inequality, evaluates the bounds, and concludes the limit.
difficulty_variables: whether the bounding functions are supplied or must be produced
whether the inequality must be verified in the response
whether the target is zero or another input
whether the theorem must be named
expected_solution_path: bound the oscillating factor between fixed values
multiply the inequality by the vanishing factor and record the direction of the inequality
evaluate the limits of the two bounds
observe that they agree and state the conclusion
archetypes.invariant_structure: The bounding inequality holds near the target but not necessarily at it, and the two bounds share a limit there, so the conclusion rests on the theorem rather than on direct evaluation.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically one part of a multipart free response question or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Limit determined by the squeeze theorem with its hypotheses stated
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for establishing the bounding inequality, one for the limits of the two bounds, and one for the conclusion. No official free response part in 2023 to 2025 assesses the squeeze theorem.
typical_wording: The stated inequality holds near the given input. Use it to determine the limit of the trapped function and justify your answer.

common_distractors: checking only that the function is defined at the input
checking only that the one sided limits agree and stopping there
evaluating the wrong branch at the boundary
restating the definition in place of a reason
archetypes.description: A piecewise defined function is given and the response determines whether it is continuous at a named input, naming the condition that fails when it is not.
difficulty_variables: whether the function value is defined at the boundary
whether the one sided limits agree
whether the justification must name the failed condition
whether the function is given by a rule or by a graph
expected_solution_path: evaluate the function at the named input
evaluate the left hand limit from the branch on that side
evaluate the right hand limit from the branch on that side
compare the limit with the function value
state the conclusion and name the condition that fails when it does
archetypes.invariant_structure: The named input is a boundary of the partition or a point excluded from a branch expression, so the test requires separate evaluation of the function value and of the one sided limits.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically one part of a multipart free response question or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Continuity at a point tested against the three conditions
archetypes.official_examples_notes: none in 2023 to 2025 as a standalone part [inferred]
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the value and the limit, and a separate justification point that requires naming which condition fails rather than restating the definition.
typical_wording: Determine whether the given function is continuous at the named input. Justify your answer.

common_distractors: classifying a cancelling factor as a vertical asymptote
calling a removable break a jump because the value is missing
treating any undefined point as an asymptote
classifying from the function value rather than the limits
archetypes.description: A function with one or more breaks is presented and the response classifies each break as removable, a jump, or due to a vertical asymptote.
difficulty_variables: whether a cancelling factor is present
whether an absolute value produces the jump
whether the graph or the rule is given
whether the classification must be justified
expected_solution_path: locate the inputs where the function is undefined or the rule changes
evaluate the one sided limits at each such input
classify from whether the one sided limits exist, agree, and are finite
archetypes.invariant_structure: Every break admits exactly one classification determined by the existence and finiteness of the one sided limits, and the classification does not depend on the function value.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Discontinuity classified from a rule or a graph
safe_variables: the expression or the shape of the graph
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point per classification with a reason point when justification is demanded.
typical_wording: Classify each discontinuity of the given function and give a reason for each classification.

common_distractors: matching only the two limits and ignoring the defined value
substituting the boundary into the wrong branch
solving one equation for two unknowns
reporting a value that makes the branches equal at the wrong input
archetypes.description: A piecewise rule containing one or two unknown constants is given and the response determines the constants that make the function continuous.
difficulty_variables: one unknown against two unknowns
one boundary against two boundaries
whether the branch expressions are linear
whether the response must also confirm the function value at the boundary
expected_solution_path: evaluate the one sided limit from each branch at the boundary
set the two expressions equal at the boundary
include the function value in the equality
solve for the unknown or solve the system for two unknowns
archetypes.invariant_structure: Continuity at each boundary yields exactly one equation, so the number of boundaries at which matching is demanded equals the number of equations available for the unknowns.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item or one part of a larger question.
archetypes.name: Parameter solved so that a piecewise function is continuous
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the matching equation at each boundary and one for the solution.
typical_wording: Find the value or values of the constants for which the given piecewise function is continuous.

common_distractors: naming an asymptote at a cancelled factor
writing a single two sided infinite limit when the signs differ
reporting the limit as a real number
omitting the side in the notation
archetypes.description: A rational or logarithmic expression is presented and the response locates the vertical asymptotes and states the behaviour on each side.
difficulty_variables: whether a factor cancels
whether the two sides have the same sign
whether the response must state the limits in notation
whether a logarithmic asymptote is included
expected_solution_path: factor numerator and denominator
divide out common factors and record where this was done
identify the remaining zeros of the denominator
determine the sign of the quotient on each side
write the one sided infinite limit statements
archetypes.invariant_structure: At least one zero of the original denominator cancels, so locating the asymptotes requires simplification before the sign analysis, and the two sides can carry opposite signs.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Vertical asymptote located and the one sided infinite limits stated
safe_variables: the number of zeros of the denominator
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the locations and one for the one sided behaviour stated in correct notation.
typical_wording: Find the vertical asymptotes of the graph of the given function and describe the behaviour of the function near each one.

common_distractors: writing the limit of the amount when the rate was requested
substituting infinity into the expression as though it were a number
reporting the limit of the rate as the limit of the amount
omitting the limit expression and giving only a value
archetypes.description: A function or a contextual model is given and the response writes the limit expression describing behaviour for inputs of large magnitude and evaluates it.
difficulty_variables: whether the expression as well as the value is demanded
whether the rate or the amount is the subject
whether the two ends differ
whether a radical is present
whether the setting is contextual
expected_solution_path: identify the function whose end behaviour is requested
write the limit expression as the variable increases without bound
divide by the dominant power or compare degrees
report the value
archetypes.invariant_structure: The response must produce the limit expression itself as well as its value, and the expression must name the correct function, which in a contextual setting may be the rate rather than the amount.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically one part of a multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: End behaviour described by a limit at infinity
safe_variables: the algebraic form of the model
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A separate point is awarded for the limit expression and another for its value; the expression point may be earned by the limit of either the amount or its rate, while a response presenting the limit of the amount is not eligible for the value point, and arithmetic performed with the infinity symbol is treated as scratch work (sg-25:4).
typical_wording: Write a limit expression that describes the long run behaviour of the given quantity and evaluate it.

common_distractors: asserting continuity without a reason
using the endpoints in the wrong order so the target is not between them
claiming a unique solution
naming a different theorem
locating a value rather than arguing existence
archetypes.description: A function known to be continuous or differentiable is given by a table, a graph, or a rule, and the response argues that the function attains a stated value somewhere in an interval.
difficulty_variables: whether continuity must be deduced from differentiability
whether the straddling pair must be chosen from a table
whether the theorem must be named
whether the answer must be phrased as a yes or no decision
expected_solution_path: state that the function is continuous and give the reason
display the two attained values that straddle the target
state that the target lies between them
conclude that at least one input in the open interval gives the target value
archetypes.invariant_structure: The continuity hypothesis must be established from a stated property rather than assumed, the target value must be shown to lie between two attained values, and the conclusion asserts existence without locating the input.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically one part of a multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: Existence of a solution argued from the Intermediate Value Theorem
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point is earned for stating that the function is continuous because it is differentiable or equivalent, and a bare statement that the function is continuous without that justification does not earn it; a second point requires the straddling inequality, a statement of continuity, and an affirmative answer, and the theorem need not be named although a named theorem must be the correct one (sg-25:12). The second point is available whether or not the first was earned.
typical_wording: Must there be a value in the stated open interval at which the function equals the given number? Justify your answer.

common_distractors: reporting the difference in outputs without dividing
using the wrong interval endpoints
calling the last average the exact instantaneous rate
omitting the units
archetypes.description: A quantity is given by a formula or a table and the response computes average rates of change over intervals closing on a point and describes what those averages approach.
difficulty_variables: whether a table or a formula is supplied
whether units are demanded
whether the response must state the limit form
whether the intervals are one sided
expected_solution_path: compute the average rate over each interval
record the sequence of values
state the value the averages approach
name that value as the instantaneous rate at the point
archetypes.invariant_structure: The averages are computed over a nested family of intervals containing the point of interest, and the response must separate the average rate over an interval from the rate at the instant.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically one part of a multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: Instantaneous rate approached through average rates over shrinking intervals
archetypes.official_examples_notes: none in 2023 to 2025 as a standalone part [inferred]
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the average rates with supporting work and one for the description of what they approach.
typical_wording: Compute the average rate of change over each of the given intervals and describe what these values indicate about the rate at the named instant.

common_distractors: matching on the function value rather than the limit
matching a one sided statement with a two sided graph
choosing a representation that agrees away from the target input only
confusing an infinite limit with a limit at infinity
archetypes.description: A limit fact is presented in one representation and the response selects or produces the equivalent presentation in another.
difficulty_variables: graph to table against table to expression against expression to verbal
whether a one sided statement is involved
whether an infinite limit is involved
whether a graph must be produced rather than selected
expected_solution_path: read the limit behaviour from the supplied representation
state the behaviour in neutral terms
test each candidate representation against that behaviour
select or produce the one that matches
archetypes.invariant_structure: The same limit behaviour at one input is carried by all the offered representations except the distractors, so the task is conversion rather than evaluation.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Limit claim matched across graphical, numerical, and analytic representations
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the correct conversion.
typical_wording: Which of the given representations is consistent with the stated limit behaviour of f at the named input?

common_distractors: rewriting an expression that substitution already settles
applying a rewriting technique that does not fit the form
treating a nonzero number over zero as an indeterminate form
reporting that a limit does not exist without considering one sided behaviour
archetypes.description: Several limit expressions are presented and the response identifies which procedure resolves each, or resolves one after classifying it.
difficulty_variables: whether the classification must be stated
whether an indeterminate form is present
whether a one sided analysis is required
whether a limit at infinity is included
expected_solution_path: substitute the target input into each expression
classify the resulting form
name the procedure that the form calls for
carry out that procedure when a value is demanded
archetypes.invariant_structure: The expressions are chosen so that substitution settles some of them, rewriting is required for others, and at least one is an unbounded quotient, so classification precedes computation.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Procedure selected for a limit from the form of the expression
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the classification and one for the resulting value.
typical_wording: For each of the given limits, identify an appropriate method and use it to determine the limit.

common_distractors: including an excluded input inside a stated interval
writing the domain as a single interval when it has several pieces
using closed brackets at an excluded input
omitting the reason when one is demanded
archetypes.description: A function given by a rule is presented and the response states the intervals on which it is continuous.
difficulty_variables: rational against radical against logarithmic against piecewise
whether an endpoint requires a one sided argument
whether the answer must be justified by naming the family
whether the domain restriction is stated in the question
expected_solution_path: identify every input at which the expression is undefined
state the family to which the expression belongs and that it is continuous on its domain
write the maximal intervals of continuity
treat any endpoint with the appropriate one sided limit
archetypes.invariant_structure: The function belongs to families continuous on their domains, so the intervals of continuity are the maximal intervals of the domain, and every excluded input must be found from the rule.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Typically a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Intervals of continuity determined from the domain of an expression
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point for the intervals and one for the reason naming the family and its domain.
typical_wording: State the intervals on which the given function is continuous and give a reason for your answer.
